stories.title: Microsoft Will Soon Release an AI Super App
stories.simple_summary: Microsoft is creating one big app that combines all its AI tools (like Copilot) into one place instead of having them scattered around.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use Microsoft products, you might find AI tools easier to find and use in one spot, but this won't change much about how the AI works.

stories.title: China warns of retaliation if US sticks with robot ban
stories.simple_summary: China is warning the U.S. that if America restricts selling robots to China, China will fight back with its own restrictions.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and large companies — nothing you need to act on as a small business owner or retiree.

stories.title: Microsoft is openly competing with OpenAI, Anthropic more than ever
stories.simple_summary: Microsoft is now building and selling its own AI tools to compete directly with other major AI companies like OpenAI.
stories.why_it_matters: This means Microsoft customers will have more AI choices available to them, but the technical details mostly matter to investors.

stories.title: The U.S. wants Asia to use its AI — but China dominates cheaper models
stories.simple_summary: The U.S. government wants Asian countries to use American-made AI, but Chinese AI tools are cheaper and winning customers instead.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a business and political story — unless you're buying AI tools internationally, it won't affect you directly.

stories.title: Mark Zuckerberg predicts that billions of people will have personal AI agents in five years
stories.simple_summary: Mark Zuckerberg says that in five years, billions of people will have personal AI assistants (similar to having a helper you can talk to) as Meta invests heavily in this technology.
stories.why_it_matters: This prediction is mostly for investors to consider — it's too far away to act on now, and personal AI assistants are still experimental.

stories.title: Microsoft logs $3.2B from Anthropic investment, but OpenAI was a mixed bag
stories.simple_summary: Microsoft made $3.2 billion from its investment in Anthropic (an AI company), though its OpenAI investment has been less clear.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors watching Microsoft's money — nothing you need to act on.

stories.title: Zuckerberg says Meta’s enterprise AI opportunity extends beyond agents
stories.simple_summary: Meta says it sees business opportunities beyond just AI agents, including AI tools that other companies can use and rent computer power from them.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a company trying to explain its business plans to investors — it won't change much for everyday users or small business owners yet.

stories.title: Microsoft confirms Copilot ‘super app’ coming this year
stories.simple_summary: Microsoft confirmed it's releasing a powerful AI app this year that can chat, write code, and perform tasks automatically across its products.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use Microsoft products for work, you may have new AI-powered features available to help you get things done faster, but the actual usefulness depends on your specific needs.

stories.title: Mark Zuckerberg is planning a big push into personal AI agents
stories.simple_summary: Meta is planning to create AI assistants that can do tasks for you automatically, like a personal helper that works online.
stories.why_it_matters: Meta is investing heavily in this, but personal AI helpers are still new — wait and see if they actually work well before considering using one.

stories.title: Elon Musk's xAI sues Minnesota over its first-in-the-nation law banning 'nudification' technology
stories.simple_summary: Elon Musk's AI company (xAI) is suing Minnesota over a new law that bans technology that creates fake nude images of people.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a legal dispute between a company and a state — nothing you need to worry about as a regular person or small business owner.

stories.title: Discover what’s next for AI, from the SaaS reckoning to the agent security gap, at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026
stories.simple_summary: TechCrunch is advertising a tech conference where people will discuss the latest AI trends and problems.
stories.why_it_matters: This is just an advertisement for a conference — unless you're looking to attend tech industry events, you don't need to act on this.

stories.title: Thinking Machines co-founder Lilian Weng left the company citing health reasons, then joined OpenAI
stories.simple_summary: A leader at an AI safety company left her job for health reasons and then took a job at OpenAI, another major AI company.
stories.why_it_matters: This is news for AI industry watchers — it doesn't affect you unless you're tracking which experts work where in the AI field.
